subject: Meteorology
title: Flash Flooding from Storms
description: A quick, practical guide to Flash Flooding from Storms.

hook.text: Flash floods kill more people in the US than tornadoes—and most start with slow-moving or training thunderstorms.

buildup.text: Training storms move over the same area repeatedly—like boxcars on a train, each dropping heavy rain in sequence.

discovery.text: Rainfall rates can exceed 100 mm per hour—overwhelming drainage systems within minutes.

twist.text: Urban areas flood faster—concrete can't absorb water, so runoff surges instantly into streets and underpasses.

climax.text: 'Turn around, don't drown' exists because most flash flood deaths occur in vehicles attempting to cross floods.

punchline.text: Six inches of fast water can knock you down—two feet can carry a car.

quiz.question: What is 'training' in the context of flash floods?
options: Storms repeatedly passing over the same area
